chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who bequeathed to another, and the beneficiary was absent, then the one who was bequeathed to died before the testator. He said: The bequest belongs to the heir of the one who was bequeathed to.

He said: Whoever bequeaths to someone, whether present or absent, and the beneficiary dies before the testator, then the bequest belongs to the heir of the one who was bequeathed to, unless he (the testator) retracts his bequest before his death.

key_terms.الغائب: Absent one — someone not physically present
key_terms.الموصى له: The beneficiary/legatee — the one in whose favour the bequest is made
key_terms.الموصي: The testator — the one who makes the bequest
key_terms.الوارث: Heir — one who inherits by legal entitlement
key_terms.الوصية: Bequest, will, testamentary disposition — a declaration of transfer of property to take effect after death
key_terms.يرجع: Retract/revoke — the testator's right to cancel the bequest before death

ai.seo_question: What happens to a bequest if the beneficiary dies before the testator in Shia law?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling attributed to Imam Ali (AS) and transmitted through Imam al-Baqir (AS) on the law of bequest (wasiyyah) when the beneficiary predeceases the testator. The ruling establishes that in such a case, the bequest does not lapse but instead passes to the heirs of the deceased beneficiary, and this applies whether the beneficiary was present or absent at the time of the bequest. The sole exception is if the testator revokes the bequest before his own death, preserving the testator's right of revocation as a check on the transfer.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Hameed, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a man who bequeathed to another, and the beneficial of it was absent. So the one who was the beneficiary who was bequeathed to, died before the testator. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The bequest is for the inheritors of the one who was bequeathed to’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who bequeaths to someone, either he is present or absent, so the beneficiary of it dies before the testator, so the bequest is for the inheritors of the one who was the beneficiary of it, except if he (the testator) were to retract in his bequest before he dies’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu Najran from ‘Asem ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays who has narrated the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin once issued a judgment, about the case of a man who made a will and the beneficiary who was absent, died before the testator, that the benefit belongs to the heir of the beneficiary.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘If one makes a will, regardless of his absence or presence, if the beneficiary dies before the testator, the benefit belongs to the heir of the beneficiary unless the testator changes his will before his death.’”
